policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV opens 'And a great multitude followed him'; a sentence-initial 'And' renders either postpositive δέ or καί, so the connective is not distinguished.
ASV 'they beheld the signs which he did' — 'beheld' is ASV's rendering of θεωρέω (ἐθεώρουν), and there is no possessive answering the αὐτοῦ of the ἑώρων αὐτοῦ reading ('his signs').
An added Greek article carries no separate English wording; ASV 'into the mountain' and 'Jesus' read the same either way.
Word order of subject and object within the Greek clause; ASV 'Jesus therefore lifting up his eyes' is idiomatic English order and does not report the Greek sequence.
An added article before the proper name Φίλιππον is not rendered in English; ASV 'saith unto Philip' fits both.
Deliberative subjunctive against future indicative; ASV 'Whence are we to buy bread' is compatible with either, and the two forms differ only by a vowel.
An added article before Φίλιππος has no English exponent; ASV 'Philip answered him' fits both.
ASV 'that every one may take a little' has no partitive answering αὐτῶν ('every one of them'), though it does render the preceding αὐτοῖς as 'for them'.
βραχύ τι and βραχύ alike yield ASV 'a little'; the enclitic is not separately rendered.
ASV 'There is a lad here' — the English indefinite article can render either the bare παιδάριον or παιδάριον ἕν.
Relative gender only: masculine ὅς by sense or neuter ὅ by grammatical agreement with παιδάριον both come into English as 'who' of a person.

ASV 'Jesus said, Make the people sit down' begins asyndetically, with no connective answering the added δέ, while the verse's other connectives are rendered ('Now there was much grass', 'So the men sat down').
ὡς and ὡσεί both give ASV 'about five thousand'.
ASV 'Jesus therefore took the loaves' renders οὖν as 'therefore'; δέ would not yield it.
ASV 'he distributed to them that were set down' has Jesus distribute directly, with nothing answering 'to the disciples, and the disciples' of the longer reading.
Verb number only, with a neuter plural subject; ASV 'which remained over' shows no number for the verb.
ASV text reads the singular 'the sign which he did', and its note 'Some ancient authorities read signs' is precisely this variant, placing the plural in the margin and the singular in the text.
ASV 'the sign which he did, they said' names no subject for the sign; there is nothing answering the added ὁ Ἰησοῦς.
ASV 'to make him king' needs an English object regardless, and the base reading already supplies the referent from 'take him by force'; the added αὐτόν is not distinguished.
ASV 'withdrew again into the mountain' renders πάλιν; the omitting reading leaves 'again' unaccounted for.
An added Greek article before πλοῖον is not distinguishable in ASV 'entered into a boat'.
ASV 'Jesus had not yet come to them' renders οὔπω 'not yet'; plain οὐκ would give 'had not come'.
Orthographic variation in the augment of the same verb; ASV 'the sea was rising' renders both alike.
Word order of verb and subject only; ASV 'the boat was at the land' follows English order either way.
ASV builds the sentence on a finite verb — 'the multitude that stood on the other side of the sea saw that there was no other boat there' — matching εἶδον, not the participle ἰδών.
ASV 'save one' stops there; nothing answers 'that one whereinto his disciples entered' of the longer reading.
ASV renders both occurrences 'boat', and the single note 'Greek little boat' is already answered by the undisputed πλοιάριον earlier in the verse, so this second word is not distinguished.
ASV 'howbeit there came boats from Tiberias' renders the adversative ἀλλά and has no 'other' modifying 'boats', which both ἄλλα readings would require.
ASV's note on 'boats' reads 'Greek little boats', naming the diminutive πλοιάρια rather than πλοῖα.
ASV's note on 'the boats' reads 'Greek little boats', naming the diminutive πλοιάρια rather than πλοῖα.
An added article before Ἰησοῦς has no English exponent; ASV 'Jesus answered and said unto them' fits both.
Present against aorist subjunctive after ἵνα; ASV 'that ye believe on him' shows no aspect. The mapped note is classed alternative_rendering and concerns 'he hath sent'.

ASV renders the simple past 'It was not Moses that gave you the bread out of heaven', where the perfect δέδωκεν would give 'hath given' in ASV's usage — as it does for the perfect in v.39, 'all that which he hath given me'.
ASV 'Jesus said unto them' is asyndetic, with nothing answering either the added οὖν ('therefore') or δέ.
Emphatic against enclitic first-person pronoun; ASV 'he that cometh to me' renders both as 'me'.
Future indicative against aorist subjunctive after οὐ μή; ASV 'shall never thirst' renders either.
Emphatic against enclitic pronoun; ASV 'shall come unto me' renders both as 'me'.
ASV reads 'I am come down from heaven' here, reserving 'out of heaven' for ἐκ (as in the same chapter's 'I am come down out of heaven'); the 'from' answers ἀπό.
ASV 'the will of him that sent me' leaves the sender unnamed; the added πατρός would give 'of the Father that sent me'.
Bare dative of time against ἐν with the dative; ASV 'at the last day' renders either.
ASV 'For this is the will of my Father' renders γάρ; δέ would not give 'for'.
ASV 'the will of my Father' matches πατρός μου; the alternative reads 'of him that sent me', which ASV does not have here.
Bare dative of time against ἐν with the dative; ASV 'at the last day' renders either.
Οὐχ and Οὐχί are the same interrogative negative; ASV 'Is not this Jesus' renders both.
ASV 'how doth he now say' renders νῦν as 'now'; οὖν would give an inferential 'then/therefore', which ASV does not have.
ASV 'how doth he now say' supplies only a pronoun subject; nothing answers the added οὗτος ('this man'), which ASV does render where it stands ('Is not this Jesus').
ASV 'Jesus answered and said unto them' has no 'therefore' answering the added οὖν.
Emphatic against enclitic pronoun; ASV 'come to me' renders both.
ASV 'Every one that hath heard from the Father' has no connective answering the added οὖν.

ASV 'Every one that hath heard from the Father, and hath learned' renders both participles as completed action, matching the aorist ἀκούσας paired with μαθών; the present ἀκούων would give 'that heareth'.
Emphatic against enclitic pronoun; ASV 'cometh unto me' renders both.
Order of verb and indefinite subject only; ASV 'Not that any man hath seen the Father' does not report the Greek sequence.
ASV 'He that believeth hath eternal life' has an absolute participle, with nothing answering the added εἰς ἐμέ ('on me').
Order of object and prepositional phrase only; ASV 'ate the manna in the wilderness' follows English order either way.
Active against middle future of ζάω; ASV 'he shall live for ever' renders both.
ASV has 'which I will give' once — 'the bread which I will give is my flesh, for the life of the world' — with nothing answering the longer reading's repeated ἣν ἐγὼ δώσω.
ASV 'give us his flesh to eat' renders the possessive αὐτοῦ, which the omitting reading lacks.
ASV's note on 'meat indeed' reads 'Greek true meat', an adjective qualifying the noun (ἀληθής βρῶσις), not the adverb ἀληθῶς ('is truly meat').
ASV's note on 'drink indeed' reads 'Greek true drink', an adjective qualifying the noun (ἀληθής πόσις), not the adverb ἀληθῶς.
Active against middle future of ζάω; ASV 'shall live because of me' renders both.
Presence of the article with οὐρανοῦ after the preposition; ASV 'out of heaven' renders both.
ASV 'not as the fathers ate, and died' has neither 'your' nor 'the manna' as object, both of which the longer reading supplies.
Active against middle future of ζάω; ASV 'shall live for ever' renders both.
Position of the demonstrative with the noun; ASV 'This is a hard saying' renders both orders alike.
ASV 'the words that I have spoken unto you' renders the perfect λελάληκα; the present λαλῶ would give 'that I speak'.
ASV 'except it be given unto him of the Father' has no possessive answering the added μου ('of my Father').
ἐκ τούτου and τούτου alike yield ASV 'Upon this'.
Order of the partitive phrase and the verb only; ASV 'many of his disciples went back' follows English order either way.
ASV 'Simon Peter answered him' has no 'therefore' answering the added οὖν.
ASV 'thou art the Holy One of God' renders ὁ ἅγιος; the alternative reads 'the Christ, the Son of God', which ASV does not have.
ASV ends 'of God'; nothing answers the added τοῦ ζῶντος ('the living').
ASV 'Judas the son of Simon Iscariot' attaches Iscariot to Simon, matching the genitive Ἰσκαριώτου; the accusative Ἰσκαριώτην would attach it to Judas.
Order of infinitive and object only; ASV 'that should betray him' follows English order either way.
ASV 'being one of the twelve' supplies a participle that English apposition requires in any case, so the added ὤν is not distinguished.
